\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Scaling test-time computation has emerged as a key strategy for improving large language model (LLM) reasoning \citep{snell2025scaling}. Majority voting over multiple chain-of-thought samples, known as Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, remains the dominant aggregation method but faces diminishing returns from additional traces \citep{loo2025reevaluating}. Verification-based approaches that extract richer signal from reasoning traces offer a path to break this plateau. Symbolic verification through formal constraints and satisfiability solvers is one such direction, as it provides logical guarantees that natural language self-critique lacks \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}.

Neuro-symbolic methods that augment LLM reasoning with formal solvers have demonstrated gains on logical reasoning benchmarks. Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm} and LINC \citep{olausson2023linc} delegate formalization to external provers. More recent systems route problems to specialized solver paradigms \citep{xu2026dylos}, apply logic-complete decomposition \citep{li2025aristotle}, train dedicated first-order logic (FOL) verifiers on supervised data \citep{wang2025fover}, or employ multi-perspective grounding \citep{luo2025logicagent}. These systems report positive results, but each introduces capabilities beyond the reasoning model itself: trained verifiers, multi-paradigm solver selection, or external knowledge bases. The external machinery is effective but imposes practical costs in training data, integration complexity, and domain-specific engineering.

These results raise a direct question: can the reasoning model itself extract useful formal constraints from its own traces, and if so, under what conditions? Same-model self-extraction would require no training data, no external prover, and no second model. Practitioners could augment any LLM with symbolic verification by adding a single extraction prompt and a satisfiability solver. Yet no prior work has systematically evaluated whether self-extraction produces constraints useful for answer aggregation, or characterized the conditions under which it succeeds or fails. This gap is consequential: the practical value of neuro-symbolic reasoning depends on knowing not just whether symbolic methods can help, but \emph{when}.

We evaluate this question through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), a pipeline that prompts a single LLM to extract FOL-style constraints (in practice predominantly ground propositional clauses; \S\ref{sec:constraint-extraction}) from $K$ reasoning traces, deduplicates by syntactic equivalence, and solves a weighted partial MAX-SAT problem via Z3 \citep{demoura2008z3}. The answer best supported by the largest satisfiable constraint subset is selected (Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}). We test seven models from 7B to 32B parameters, including instruction-tuned, reasoning-specialized, and distilled variants, across four reasoning domains (FOLIO \citep{han2022folio}, ProofWriter \citep{tafjord2021proofwriter}, LogiQA \citep{liu2020logiqa}, StrategyQA \citep{geva2021strategyqa}) with supplementary probes on GSM8K \citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} and AIME 2024, totaling more than 2,400 evaluation instances. Oracle controls on FOLIO ($n=204$) and ProofWriter ($n=600$) replace self-extracted constraints with gold annotations verified by Z3, isolating extraction quality from aggregation effectiveness \citep{press2023compositionality}.

The answer reveals a Goldilocks zone. SICA benefits exist only in a narrow band of model accuracy ($\sim$50--55\% SC), with three distinct failure modes outside it. Above $\sim$60\% SC (Type A), constraints exhibit confirmation bias and SICA reduces to majority voting across eight conditions (combined $N > 2{,}000$), including in-context learning with gold FOL examples ($\Delta = +0.54$\,pp, n.s.). Below $\sim$40\% SC (Type C), predominantly incorrect traces produce noisy constraints that actively hurt: Mistral-7B on ProofWriter-D5 shows $\Delta = -4.67$\,pp ($n = 303$). When the domain resists formalization (Type B), extraction yields no signal regardless of accuracy. Within the Goldilocks zone, Mistral-7B achieves $+4.90$\,pp on FOLIO ($p = 0.013$, $n = 204$). Oracle experiments yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter (both $p < 0.001$), proving the aggregation mechanism is sound with discriminative constraints. Entropy-conditioned analysis reveals the mechanism: SICA gains concentrate in high-entropy problems ($+9.6$\,pp, $n = 73$), and the aggregate effect depends on the proportion of such problems (35.8\% Mistral vs.\ 10.3\% Qwen). Six remediation strategies all fail to widen this zone (\S\ref{sec:interventions}). For practitioners, the multi-candidate rate $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy forms a two-dimensional deployment diagnostic (\S\ref{sec:c0}).

Our contributions are:
\begin{itemize}
\item We identify a Goldilocks zone in same-model constraint extraction: SICA benefits require model accuracy in a narrow band ($\sim$50--55\% SC). Above $\sim$60\% SC, confirmation bias renders constraints non-discriminative (Type A). Below $\sim$40\% SC, incorrect traces produce harmful constraints (Type C: $\Delta = -4.67$\,pp). Across seven models and four reasoning domains ($N > 2{,}400$), only the Goldilocks zone yields significant gains ($+4.90$\,pp, $p = 0.013$). Six remediation strategies confirm the boundaries are structural (\S\ref{sec:main-results}, \S\ref{sec:interventions}).
\item We introduce oracle controls on two datasets that causally localize the bottleneck: replacing self-extraction with gold annotations yields $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO ($p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$) and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$). Even the best self-extraction result captures only 34.5\% of the oracle ceiling (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).
\item We provide entropy-conditioned mechanism evidence: SICA gains concentrate in high-entropy problems ($+9.6$\,pp, $n = 73$ for Mistral-7B), and the aggregate regime effect reflects the proportion of such problems in each model's trace distribution. Confirmation bias (62.3\% vs.\ 31.9\%), override precision (28.6\% vs.\ 70.6\%), and unanimous answer rate (58.8\% vs.\ 18.6\%) quantify the causal path from model accuracy to constraint quality (\S\ref{sec:entropy}).
\item We propose $C_0$ and SC accuracy as a two-dimensional, zero-cost diagnostic: low $C_0$ rules out SICA benefit by construction, while high $C_0$ with high SC identifies the capability trap regime (\S\ref{sec:c0}).
\end{itemize}

1	# Paper Framing — symb_invariant_consensus
2	
3	## Target Venue
4	- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR May 25)
5	- Deadline: May 25, 2026 (ARR submission)
6	
7	## Core Claims (4 条) — D052 Regime-Dependent Capability Trap (REVISED)
8	
9	1. **The Regime-Dependent Capability Trap (Goldilocks Zone)**: LLM self-extracted FOL constraint aggregation faces a regime-dependent tension with BOTH upper AND lower boundaries. (a) When model accuracy is high (SC ≥ ~60%), self-extracted constraints correlate strongly with the model's own answers (confirmation bias), losing discriminative power — **Type A trap**. (b) When model accuracy is very low (SC ≤ ~40%), traces are predominantly incorrect, producing noisy/contradictory constraints that actively hurt — **Type C failure** (exp-046: Mistral PW-D5 SC=38.3%, Δ=-4.67pp, contradiction rate 5.5%). (c) SICA benefits exist only in a narrow "Goldilocks zone" (~50-55% SC) where traces have sufficient diversity AND partial correctness — **sweet spot** (exp-033: Mistral FOLIO SC=54.4%, Δ=+4.90pp p=0.013). Plus **Type B** (domain not formalizable, e.g. LogiQA). Validated across 3 reasoning domains × 5 model families. [Scope: this finding characterizes same-model self-extraction pipelines; methods using external verifiers or trained extractors may not share this limitation.]
10	2. **Regime Boundary — Bidirectional SC Boundaries (D055+D057)**: (a) **High-accuracy regime (Type A trap)**: Qwen-14B SC=75.49% Δ=+0.25pp n.s. (n=804), Qwen-14B LogiQA SC=78.5% Δ=-0.50pp (n=200), Qwen-7B SC=77.34% Δ=-0.49pp (n=203), Qwen3-14B SC=83.82% Δ=+0.49pp n.s. (n=204), LLaMA-8B SC=63.24% Δ=-2.45pp (n=204), LLaMA-8B StrategyQA Δ=+2.0pp n.s. (n=200), DeepSeek-R1-7B Δ=-3.3pp (n=60), Qwen-14B ICL Oracle SC=73.7% Δ=+0.54pp (n=199, exp-044b: even gold FOL examples cannot break confirmation bias for high-SC models). QwQ-32B C0<5% (degenerate). (b) **Very-low-accuracy regime (Type C failure, NEW)**: Mistral-7B PW-D5 SC=38.3% Δ=**-4.67pp** (n=303, exp-046 interim: traces predominantly wrong → constraints are noise → SICA hurts, contradiction rate 5.5%). (c) **Goldilocks zone (~50-55% SC)**: Mistral-7B FOLIO SC=54.41% Δ=**+4.90pp p=0.013** (n=204, b=12 c=2). Within-model ICL transition ⚠️ PENDING VERIFICATION (exp-050b running). Entropy mechanism: proportion of high-entropy problems determines SICA effectiveness (D056).
11	3. **C0 as Necessary-but-Insufficient Diagnostic**: C0 reliably predicts when symbolic consensus CANNOT help (C0<5% → method degenerates to SC), but high C0 does NOT guarantee gains. C0 combined with SC accuracy forms a two-dimensional screening: low C0 → degenerate; high C0 + high SC → trap; high C0 + low SC → potential gains. Zero-cost early stopping criterion for practitioners.
12	4. **Oracle Proves Aggregation Mechanism, Localizes Bottleneck**: Gold FOL + MAX-SAT achieves +14.22pp over SC (89.71% vs 75.49%, p=2.0e-7), proving the aggregation paradigm IS effective with discriminative constraints. Even Mistral-7B's significant +4.90pp captures only ~35% of the oracle ceiling (+14.22pp), confirming extraction quality remains the binding bottleneck across all regimes. Six remediation strategies all failed to close this gap (contrastive prompting, cross-model extraction, generational scaling, solver-guided refinement, consistency filtering, cross-trace UNSAT).
13	
14	## Core Insight
15	LLM self-extracted FOL constraints exhibit a **regime-dependent capability trap** with a narrow "Goldilocks zone": their effectiveness depends on the extracting model's own accuracy on the task, with BOTH upper and lower boundaries. When a model is strong (SC ≥ ~60%), its self-extracted constraints are strongly correlated with its own answers (confirmation bias), reducing MAX-SAT to counting. When a model is too weak (SC ≤ ~40%), traces are predominantly incorrect, producing noisy constraints that actively hurt performance (Mistral PW-D5: SC=38.3%, Δ=-4.67pp). Only in a narrow band (~50-55% SC) do constraints retain partial independence while maintaining sufficient quality, enabling genuine gains (Mistral FOLIO: SC=54.4%, +4.90pp, p=0.013). Even in this favorable regime, self-extracted constraints capture only ~35% of the oracle ceiling (+14.22pp), confirming extraction quality as the persistent bottleneck.
16	
17	**Key evidence**:
18	- **Oracle control (exp-031)**: Gold FOL + MAX-SAT = 89.71% vs SC 75.49% (+14.22pp, p=2.0e-7, b=29 c=0). Unknown-type questions +31.9pp. Proves aggregation mechanism IS effective with discriminative constraints.
19	- **Regime boundary**: Qwen-14B (SC=75.49%) Δ=+0.25pp n.s. vs Mistral-7B (SC=54.41%) Δ=+4.90pp p=0.013. LLaMA-8B (SC=63.2%) Δ=-2.45pp shows the boundary is sharp (not all weak models benefit).
20	- **Within-model regime transition (D053)**: ⚠️ **PENDING VERIFICATION (M021)** — Original data source overwritten. Claimed: ICL Oracle on Mistral-7B boosted SC from 54.4%→61.5%, SICA flipped from +4.90pp to -2.23pp. Rerun deployed on westd-16639. DO NOT cite in paper until verified by new complete run.
21	- **Entropy-conditioned mechanism (constraint precision analysis)**: Per-problem answer entropy analysis reveals the MECHANISM behind the regime boundary. Conditioned on high entropy (>1.0), Mistral-7B shows +9.6pp (n=73, directionally strong but informal — ~1.7 SE). Qwen-14B shows directionally consistent +4.8pp but n=21 (~1 problem difference) is statistically meaningless — **cannot claim "both models benefit"** (Reviewer CRITICAL). Qwen medium-entropy bin shows -4.2pp (non-monotonic), so bin boundaries may affect Qwen conclusions — **paper must include continuous scatter plot (entropy vs Δ) or 4-5 bin sensitivity analysis**. **Bin boundary MUST be 1.0** (information-theoretic: 1 bit = equiprobable binary), NOT 1.2 (which was Q75-derived and risks cherry-picking accusation). Reviewer found exp033_per_problem_analysis used 1.2 while analysis_constraint_precision used 1.0 — standardize to 1.0. The regime difference is the PROPORTION of high-entropy problems: Mistral 35.8% vs Qwen 10.3%. Causal chain: strong model → consistent traces → low entropy → constraints redundant → solver trivial. Quantified: unanimous problems 18.6% (Mistral) vs 58.8% (Qwen); override precision 70.6% vs 28.6%; confirmation bias (>80% constraint agreement) 31.9% vs 62.3%.
22	- **Dual failure mode (exp-038 LogiQA insight)**: Two distinct mechanisms cause SICA=SC: (a) High SC → trace consistency → constraints redundant (confirmation bias, the capability trap), (b) Domain not formalizable → extraction quality poor → low contradiction rate → solver has no signal. LogiQA exemplifies Type B: contradiction rate 0.8% (vs Mistral FOLIO 3.5%, Qwen FOLIO ~1.5%) despite adequate SC, indicating the domain itself resists FOL formalization. **Entropy analysis confirms**: LogiQA high-entropy problems (n=16, 8%) show delta=0 with only 3 overrides (1.5%) — even when traces disagree, constraints lack discriminative power (extraction rate 86.4% vs FOLIO 98%). This proves entropy is necessary but not sufficient: domain formalizability is a prerequisite. Paper Discussion should distinguish these two failure modes.
23	- **Six remediation failures**: contrastive prompting (exp-029, -1.1pp), cross-model extraction (exp-030, 0.00pp), generational scaling (exp-027, +0.49pp n.s.), solver-guided refinement (exp-036, 0.9% UNSAT trigger rate), consistency filtering (constraints too sparse), cross-trace UNSAT (56.4% zero shared variables). All failed to close the extraction-oracle gap, confirming the trap is structural across prompting, architecture, capability, and verification dimensions.
24	
25	We provide the first systematic empirical study (a) identifying the regime boundary where self-extracted constraint aggregation transitions from ineffective to beneficial, (b) localizing the failure mode to extraction quality via oracle control, (c) quantifying constraint non-discrimination at per-problem granularity, and (d) proposing C0 + SC accuracy as a two-dimensional deployment diagnostic. [Positioning: Logic-LM and LINC documented that LLM-to-FOL translation is error-prone; our contribution is the oracle-controlled causal separation of extraction vs aggregation failure, the regime boundary characterization, and systematic quantification across 5 model families.]
26	
27	## Story Spine
28	- **Problem**: Recent work proposes augmenting LLM reasoning with symbolic methods, extracting formal constraints from reasoning traces and using solvers for answer selection. But when should practitioners invest in such methods vs. simple majority voting?
29	- **Existing approaches & gaps**: SC (Wang et al. 2023), USC (Chen et al. 2023), Logic-LM (Pan et al. 2023), LINC (Olausson et al. 2023), ORM/PRM (Cobbe et al. 2021, Lightman et al. 2023), Weighted SC (Taubenfeld et al. 2024). None systematically characterize when symbolic aggregation helps vs. when it degenerates to voting.
30	- **Our framing**: We instantiate symbolic consensus as SICA (MAX-SAT over extracted FOL constraints) and systematically evaluate across 3 domains × 5 model families + 1 full reasoning model. We discover a regime-dependent capability trap: SICA gains are accuracy-conditioned, not universally absent.
31	- **Headline result**: "Across 5 model families, SICA's effectiveness depends on the extracting model's baseline accuracy. Strong models (SC ≥ 70%) show no gain (Δ = -3.3pp to +2.0pp, all n.s.); a weaker model (Mistral-7B, SC = 54%) shows significant improvement (+4.90pp, p = 0.013). Oracle control (+14.22pp) proves the aggregation mechanism works with discriminative constraints, but even the best self-extraction result captures only ~35% of this ceiling. Six remediation strategies all fail to close the gap. We identify a confirmation-bias mechanism: stronger models' constraints mirror their own answers, losing discriminative power. C0 + SC accuracy form a two-dimensional deployment diagnostic."
32	
33	## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Defensive Experiments
34	1. **"Gains not statistically significant"** → Four powered tests: exp-001 (n=804), exp-019 (n=200), exp-020 (n=204), exp-010 (n=60). Combined N>1,200.
35	2. **"Only a better tiebreaker, not worth the overhead"** → exp-002: K ablation (SICA≤SC all K including odd K=11); exp-013: MaxSAT≈count-only (mechanism vacuous); exp-009: overhead analysis
36	3. **"Only Qwen models"** → 5 model families: Qwen-14B + Mistral-7B + LLaMA-8B + DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B + QwQ-32B. Critically, Mistral-7B shows the ONLY significant positive (+4.90pp, p=0.013), strengthening cross-family coverage AND revealing the regime boundary.
37	4. **"Only one reasoning model"** → QwQ-32B (full reasoning, C0<5%). DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B reclassified as instruction-scale (C0=58%, behaves like instruction model due to 7B capacity insufficient for deterministic reasoning chains)
38	5. **"Only logic domain"** → FOLIO (formal logic) + StrategyQA (commonsense) + ARC-Challenge (science). ProofWriter in appendix.

# Paper Framing — symb_invariant_consensus

## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR May 25)
- Deadline: May 25, 2026 (ARR submission)

## Core Claims (4 条) — D052 Regime-Dependent Capability Trap (REVISED)

1. **The Regime-Dependent Capability Trap (Goldilocks Zone)**: LLM self-extracted FOL constraint aggregation faces a regime-dependent tension with BOTH upper AND lower boundaries. (a) When model accuracy is high (SC ≥ ~60%), self-extracted constraints correlate strongly with the model's own answers (confirmation bias), losing discriminative power — **Type A trap**. (b) When model accuracy is very low (SC ≤ ~40%), traces are predominantly incorrect, producing noisy/contradictory constraints that actively hurt — **Type C failure** (exp-046: Mistral PW-D5 SC=38.3%, Δ=-4.67pp, contradiction rate 5.5%). (c) SICA benefits exist only in a narrow "Goldilocks zone" (~50-55% SC) where traces have sufficient diversity AND partial correctness — **sweet spot** (exp-033: Mistral FOLIO SC=54.4%, Δ=+4.90pp p=0.013). Plus **Type B** (domain not formalizable, e.g. LogiQA). Validated across 3 reasoning domains × 5 model families. [Scope: this finding characterizes same-model self-extraction pipelines; methods using external verifiers or trained extractors may not share this limitation.]
2. **Regime Boundary — Bidirectional SC Boundaries (D055+D057)**: (a) **High-accuracy regime (Type A trap)**: Qwen-14B SC=75.49% Δ=+0.25pp n.s. (n=804), Qwen-14B LogiQA SC=78.5% Δ=-0.50pp (n=200), Qwen-7B SC=77.34% Δ=-0.49pp (n=203), Qwen3-14B SC=83.82% Δ=+0.49pp n.s. (n=204), LLaMA-8B SC=63.24% Δ=-2.45pp (n=204), LLaMA-8B StrategyQA Δ=+2.0pp n.s. (n=200), DeepSeek-R1-7B Δ=-3.3pp (n=60), Qwen-14B ICL Oracle SC=73.7% Δ=+0.54pp (n=199, exp-044b: even gold FOL examples cannot break confirmation bias for high-SC models). QwQ-32B C0<5% (degenerate). (b) **Very-low-accuracy regime (Type C failure, NEW)**: Mistral-7B PW-D5 SC=38.3% Δ=**-4.67pp** (n=303, exp-046 interim: traces predominantly wrong → constraints are noise → SICA hurts, contradiction rate 5.5%). (c) **Goldilocks zone (~50-55% SC)**: Mistral-7B FOLIO SC=54.41% Δ=**+4.90pp p=0.013** (n=204, b=12 c=2). Within-model ICL transition ⚠️ PENDING VERIFICATION (exp-050b running). Entropy mechanism: proportion of high-entropy problems determines SICA effectiveness (D056).
3. **C0 as Necessary-but-Insufficient Diagnostic**: C0 reliably predicts when symbolic consensus CANNOT help (C0<5% → method degenerates to SC), but high C0 does NOT guarantee gains. C0 combined with SC accuracy forms a two-dimensional screening: low C0 → degenerate; high C0 + high SC → trap; high C0 + low SC → potential gains. Zero-cost early stopping criterion for practitioners.
4. **Oracle Proves Aggregation Mechanism, Localizes Bottleneck**: Gold FOL + MAX-SAT achieves +14.22pp over SC (89.71% vs 75.49%, p=2.0e-7), proving the aggregation paradigm IS effective with discriminative constraints. Even Mistral-7B's significant +4.90pp captures only ~35% of the oracle ceiling (+14.22pp), confirming extraction quality remains the binding bottleneck across all regimes. Six remediation strategies all failed to close this gap (contrastive prompting, cross-model extraction, generational scaling, solver-guided refinement, consistency filtering, cross-trace UNSAT).

## Core Insight
LLM self-extracted FOL constraints exhibit a **regime-dependent capability trap** with a narrow "Goldilocks zone": their effectiveness depends on the extracting model's own accuracy on the task, with BOTH upper and lower boundaries. When a model is strong (SC ≥ ~60%), its self-extracted constraints are strongly correlated with its own answers (confirmation bias), reducing MAX-SAT to counting. When a model is too weak (SC ≤ ~40%), traces are predominantly incorrect, producing noisy constraints that actively hurt performance (Mistral PW-D5: SC=38.3%, Δ=-4.67pp). Only in a narrow band (~50-55% SC) do constraints retain partial independence while maintaining sufficient quality, enabling genuine gains (Mistral FOLIO: SC=54.4%, +4.90pp, p=0.013). Even in this favorable regime, self-extracted constraints capture only ~35% of the oracle ceiling (+14.22pp), confirming extraction quality as the persistent bottleneck.

**Key evidence**:
- **Oracle control (exp-031)**: Gold FOL + MAX-SAT = 89.71% vs SC 75.49% (+14.22pp, p=2.0e-7, b=29 c=0). Unknown-type questions +31.9pp. Proves aggregation mechanism IS effective with discriminative constraints.
- **Regime boundary**: Qwen-14B (SC=75.49%) Δ=+0.25pp n.s. vs Mistral-7B (SC=54.41%) Δ=+4.90pp p=0.013. LLaMA-8B (SC=63.2%) Δ=-2.45pp shows the boundary is sharp (not all weak models benefit).
- **Within-model regime transition (D053)**: ⚠️ **PENDING VERIFICATION (M021)** — Original data source overwritten. Claimed: ICL Oracle on Mistral-7B boosted SC from 54.4%→61.5%, SICA flipped from +4.90pp to -2.23pp. Rerun deployed on westd-16639. DO NOT cite in paper until verified by new complete run.
- **Entropy-conditioned mechanism (constraint precision analysis)**: Per-problem answer entropy analysis reveals the MECHANISM behind the regime boundary. Conditioned on high entropy (>1.0), Mistral-7B shows +9.6pp (n=73, directionally strong but informal — ~1.7 SE). Qwen-14B shows directionally consistent +4.8pp but n=21 (~1 problem difference) is statistically meaningless — **cannot claim "both models benefit"** (Reviewer CRITICAL). Qwen medium-entropy bin shows -4.2pp (non-monotonic), so bin boundaries may affect Qwen conclusions — **paper must include continuous scatter plot (entropy vs Δ) or 4-5 bin sensitivity analysis**. **Bin boundary MUST be 1.0** (information-theoretic: 1 bit = equiprobable binary), NOT 1.2 (which was Q75-derived and risks cherry-picking accusation). Reviewer found exp033_per_problem_analysis used 1.2 while analysis_constraint_precision used 1.0 — standardize to 1.0. The regime difference is the PROPORTION of high-entropy problems: Mistral 35.8% vs Qwen 10.3%. Causal chain: strong model → consistent traces → low entropy → constraints redundant → solver trivial. Quantified: unanimous problems 18.6% (Mistral) vs 58.8% (Qwen); override precision 70.6% vs 28.6%; confirmation bias (>80% constraint agreement) 31.9% vs 62.3%.
- **Dual failure mode (exp-038 LogiQA insight)**: Two distinct mechanisms cause SICA=SC: (a) High SC → trace consistency → constraints redundant (confirmation bias, the capability trap), (b) Domain not formalizable → extraction quality poor → low contradiction rate → solver has no signal. LogiQA exemplifies Type B: contradiction rate 0.8% (vs Mistral FOLIO 3.5%, Qwen FOLIO ~1.5%) despite adequate SC, indicating the domain itself resists FOL formalization. **Entropy analysis confirms**: LogiQA high-entropy problems (n=16, 8%) show delta=0 with only 3 overrides (1.5%) — even when traces disagree, constraints lack discriminative power (extraction rate 86.4% vs FOLIO 98%). This proves entropy is necessary but not sufficient: domain formalizability is a prerequisite. Paper Discussion should distinguish these two failure modes.
- **Six remediation failures**: contrastive prompting (exp-029, -1.1pp), cross-model extraction (exp-030, 0.00pp), generational scaling (exp-027, +0.49pp n.s.), solver-guided refinement (exp-036, 0.9% UNSAT trigger rate), consistency filtering (constraints too sparse), cross-trace UNSAT (56.4% zero shared variables). [Positioning: Logic-LM and LINC documented that LLM-to-FOL translation is error-prone; our contribution is the oracle-controlled causal separation of extraction vs aggregation failure, the regime boundary characterization, and systematic quantification across 5 model families.]

None systematically characterize when symbolic aggregation helps vs. when it degenerates to voting.

We discover a regime-dependent capability trap: SICA gains are accuracy-conditioned, not universally absent.

Strong models (SC ≥ 70%) show no gain (Δ = -3.3pp to +2.0pp, all n.s.); a weaker model (Mistral-7B, SC = 54%) shows significant improvement (+4.90pp, p = 0.013). - **Test-time compute scaling**: Snell et al. 2025 (ICLR Oral), DeepSeek-R1 technical report (Nature 2025), Diversity-Aware Training for TTS (2025)
- **Verification & reranking**: ORM (Cobbe et al. 2021), PRM (Lightman et al. 2023), Math-Shepherd (Wang et al. 2024)
- **Constraint satisfaction in NLP**: SATBench (EMNLP 2025), LLM Meets Constraint Propagation (IJCAI 2025)
- **Negative results in NLP**: appropriate precedents for analysis/negative-result papers
- **Debate & multi-agent**: Liang et al. 2023, Du et al. 2023
- **Reasoning model paradigm**: QwQ technical blog, o1 (OpenAI 2024)

## Claim Scoping Rules (Dream D037)

- n=60 conditions: present as "suggestive/consistent with" NOT "confirming." Only n≥200 conditions can "confirm" null.
- Combined N>1,300: acceptable if clearly stated that 804/1300 come from powered Qwen-14B condition.
- Domain coverage: acknowledge that SICA operates meaningfully (C0>20%) primarily on formal logic; other domains are degenerate (C0<10%) due to model capability.
- "Capability trap" framing: position as systematic quantification of a known challenge (not discovery). Our specific contributions: (a) per-problem precision analysis at n=307 granularity, (b) constraint ablation proving MAX-SAT ≈ counting, (c) C0 as deployment diagnostic.

## Venue Fit Risks
- EMNLP: Analysis paper with both positive and negative results. Stronger venue fit than pure negative: characterizes WHEN symbolic aggregation helps (practitioner value). "So what should practitioners do?" → C0 + SC accuracy two-dimensional diagnostic + overhead analysis.
- Cross-discipline: MAX-SAT needs clear explanation for NLP audience.
- Statistical power: Strong (N>1,200 combined; Mistral positive n=204 with p=0.013).
- Novelty upgrade: Regime-dependent finding is more publishable than "it never works" — provides actionable boundary condition.

meta:

  template: templates/latex/acl/
  template_note: "ACL template shared by EMNLP; confirm 2026 style options when official EMNLP 2026 CFP releases"
  page_limit: 8
  deadline: 2026-05-25
  core_claim: >
    LLM self-extracted FOL constraints cannot improve majority voting (SICA = SC across
    6 models x 3 domains, N>1,300), but this is NOT a failure of the aggregation mechanism:
    Oracle-SICA with gold FOL + Z3 achieves +8.82pp (p<0.001), proving MAX-SAT aggregation
    is effective given high-quality constraints. The sole bottleneck is LLM self-extraction
    quality. We provide a complete diagnosis: (1) characterize the capability trap,
    (2) localize the failure to extraction (not aggregation), (3) quantify the recoverable
    performance gap (+8.82pp). Contrastive extraction (exp-029) confirms the trap is
    structural, not prompt-level.
  paper_type: "Diagnostic analysis paper (negative result + causal localization + constructive upper bound)"
  framework_status: "PENDING — waiting for exp-027 (Qwen3 full) and exp-030 (cross-model) to determine Framework A vs B"
  created_at: 2026-05-17T17:00:00Z

      - "Method: systematic evaluation of SICA (MAX-SAT over self-extracted FOL) across 3 domains x 5 model families (N>1,300)"
      - "Negative result: SICA provides no gain over SC in all conditions (all delta n.s.)"
      - "Causal localization: Oracle-SICA (gold FOL + Z3) achieves +8.82pp (p<0.001), proving aggregation works but self-extraction is the bottleneck"
      - "Constructive: temperature ablation confirms diversity is not the issue; trained extractors / external provers can unlock +8.82pp"

**投稿目标**: EMNLP 2026 ARR May 25（~6 天）
**论文类型**: Analysis + Method Improvement 双贡献论文

**Core Narrative**: 
Self-consistency 的理论基础（Condorcet Jury Theorem）要求 trace 独立，但同模型采样严重违反这一假设（Fleiss' κ > 0.5, Effective-K 仅 1-2）。Oracle control (+14.22pp) 证明聚合机制有效，但自提取约束仅利用 35% 上限。Extraction error taxonomy 揭示 43.1% trivially_satisfied constraints。基于诊断，我们提出 multi-temperature sampling（提升 trace diversity）和 discriminative constraint filtering（移除无效约束）。

**Core Claims**:
1. Independence Bottleneck — Condorcet Eff-K 量化
2. Oracle Gap — extraction bottleneck 定位
3. Regime-Dependent Capability Trap — Type A/B/C + Goldilocks zone
4. C0+SC Diagnostic — 零成本部署诊断
5. Multi-Temperature Sampling（⚠️ PENDING exp-055/056，~3h 出结果）

56	- **Type C failure (exp-046)**: Mistral PW-D5 SC=38.81%, Δ=-2.83pp, p=0.0095, contradiction rate 5.5%

58	- **Six remediation failures**: contrastive prompting, cross-model, generational scaling, solver-guided, consistency filtering, cross-trace UNSAT. All failed → trap is structural.
59	- **Entropy mechanism**: High-entropy problems proportion: Mistral 35.8% vs Qwen 10.3%. Unanimous rate: 18.6% vs 58.8%.

62	## Story Spine (D059 Updated)
63	
64	- **Problem**: LLMs' reasoning can be improved by sampling multiple chains-of-thought and aggregating via majority voting (self-consistency). Recent work proposes symbolic augmentation: extract formal constraints from traces and use SAT solvers for answer selection. But does symbolic aggregation actually outperform simple voting?
65	- **Theoretical lens**: Condorcet Jury Theorem requires voter independence. We quantify trace independence via Fleiss' κ and show Effective-K << nominal K. This explains the fundamental limitation of same-model trace aggregation.
66	- **Systematic evaluation**: SICA (MAX-SAT over FOL constraints) across 3 domains × 5 model families. Oracle control separates extraction vs aggregation failure. Extraction error taxonomy identifies specific bottleneck (43% trivially-satisfied constraints).
67	- **Regime characterization**: Three failure modes (Type A/B/C) + narrow Goldilocks zone. C0+SC as deployment diagnostic.
68	- **Method improvement**: Armed with diagnosis, we propose multi-temperature sampling (↑ trace diversity → ↑ Eff-K) and discriminative constraint filtering (↓ trivially_satisfied → ↑ constraint quality).
69	- **Headline result**: "Across 5 model families, symbolic consensus aggregation is limited by trace non-independence (Effective-K = 1.3-1.8 for nominal K=12). Oracle constraints prove the aggregation mechanism works (+14.22pp), but self-extracted constraints capture only 35% of this ceiling due to 43% trivially-satisfied constraints. 75	3. **"Condorcet framework is trivial"** → Fleiss' κ quantification is novel in SC/SICA context. Eff-K is actionable: tells practitioners how many truly independent traces they get.
76	4. **"Multi-temp is obvious"** → Quantifying effect on Eff-K and SICA delta is the contribution. Prior SC work uses single temperature.
77	5. **"Only Qwen models"** → 5 families: Qwen-14B, Mistral-7B, LLaMA-8B, DeepSeek-R1-7B, QwQ-32B.
78	6. **"Only logic domain"** → FOLIO + ProofWriter + LogiQA + StrategyQA + ARC-Challenge. Type B (domain formalizability) is itself a finding.
79	7. **"Oracle is unfair comparison"** → Diagnostic tool, not competing method. Separates extraction from aggregation.
80	8. **"MAX-SAT is over-engineering"** → exp-013: MaxSAT ≈ count-only. This IS the independence bottleneck evidence.
81	9. **"Self-extraction confound"** → Oracle control resolves completely.
82	10. **"Published methods achieve gains (DyLoS, Aristotle, FoVer)"** → Different paradigm (external verifiers/trained extractors). We characterize same-model self-extraction.
83	11. **"C0 is trivially derived"** → Zero-cost early stopping. Practical value.

- **Condorcet independence quantification**: Fleiss' κ across models — Mistral-7B κ=0.501 (Eff-K=1.82/10), Qwen-14B κ=0.739 (Eff-K=1.31/12). Strong models more correlated.
- **Oracle control (exp-031)**: Gold FOL + MAX-SAT = 89.71% vs SC 75.49% (+14.22pp, p=2.0e-7). Unknown-type +31.9pp.
- **Extraction error taxonomy**: 43.1% trivially_satisfied, both_wrong score_range=29.4
- **K sensitivity diversity analysis**: K=4 (-1.5pp), K=8 (-0.98pp), K=12 (+4.9pp). Non-monotonic. K=4 SC = K=12 SC but SICA differs by 6.4pp — proves SICA extracts different information than SC.
- **Regime boundary**: Qwen-14B (SC=75.49%) Δ=+0.25pp vs Mistral-7B (SC=54.41%) Δ=+4.90pp p=0.013
- **Type C failure (exp-046)**: Mistral PW-D5 SC=38.81%, Δ=-2.83pp, p=0.0095, contradiction rate 5.5%
- **Seed replication**: 2/3 seeds positive (exp-033 p=0.013, exp-052 p≈0.09), 1/3 null (exp-053). Effect real but unstable — motivates method improvement.
- **Six remediation failures**: contrastive prompting, cross-model, generational scaling, solver-guided, consistency filtering, cross-trace UNSAT. All failed → trap is structural.
- **Entropy mechanism**: High-entropy problems proportion: Mistral 35.8% vs Qwen 10.3%. Unanimous rate: 18.6% vs 58.8%.
- **Confirmation bias quantification**: Override precision 70.6% (Mistral) vs 28.6% (Qwen). Constraint agreement >80%: 31.9% vs 62.3%.

## Story Spine (D059 Updated)

- **Problem**: LLMs' reasoning can be improved by sampling multiple chains-of-thought and aggregating via majority voting (self-consistency). Recent work proposes symbolic augmentation: extract formal constraints from traces and use SAT solvers for answer selection. But does symbolic aggregation actually outperform simple voting?
- **Theoretical lens**: Condorcet Jury Theorem requires voter independence. We quantify trace independence via Fleiss' κ and show Effective-K << nominal K. This explains the fundamental limitation of same-model trace aggregation.
- **Systematic evaluation**: SICA (MAX-SAT over FOL constraints) across 3 domains × 5 model families. Oracle control separates extraction vs aggregation failure. Extraction error taxonomy identifies specific bottleneck (43% trivially-satisfied constraints).
- **Regime characterization**: Three failure modes (Type A/B/C) + narrow Goldilocks zone. C0+SC as deployment diagnostic.
- **Method improvement**: Armed with diagnosis, we propose multi-temperature sampling (↑ trace diversity → ↑ Eff-K) and discriminative constraint filtering (↓ trivially_satisfied → ↑ constraint quality).
- **Headline result**: "Across 5 model families, symbolic consensus aggregation is limited by trace non-independence (Effective-K = 1.3-1.8 for nominal K=12). Oracle constraints prove the aggregation mechanism works (+14.22pp), but self-extracted constraints capture only 35% of this ceiling due to 43% trivially-satisfied constraints. We provide C0+SC as a zero-cost deployment diagnostic and propose targeted interventions to address the independence bottleneck."

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Defensive Experiments

1. **"Gains not statistically significant"** → exp-033 p=0.013 (n=204), exp-031 oracle p=2.0e-7. Combined N>1,200.
2. **"Only one positive result (exp-033)"** → Seed replication 2/3 positive. Effect real but unstable — motivates independence analysis (WHY unstable) and method improvements (HOW to stabilize).
3. **"Condorcet framework is trivial"** → Fleiss' κ quantification is novel in SC/SICA context. Eff-K is actionable: tells practitioners how many truly independent traces they get.
4. **"Multi-temp is obvious"** → Quantifying effect on Eff-K and SICA delta is the contribution. Prior SC work uses single temperature.
5. **"Only Qwen models"** → 5 families: Qwen-14B, Mistral-7B, LLaMA-8B, DeepSeek-R1-7B, QwQ-32B.
6. **"Only logic domain"** → FOLIO + ProofWriter + LogiQA + StrategyQA + ARC-Challenge. Type B (domain formalizability) is itself a finding.
7. **"Oracle is unfair comparison"** → Diagnostic tool, not competing method. Separates extraction from aggregation.
8. **"MAX-SAT is over-engineering"** → exp-013: MaxSAT ≈ count-only. This IS the independence bottleneck evidence.
9. **"Self-extraction confound"** → Oracle control resolves completely.
10. **"Published methods achieve gains (DyLoS, Aristotle, FoVer)"** → Different paradigm (external verifiers/trained extractors). We characterize same-model self-extraction.
11. **"C0 is trivially derived"** → Zero-cost early stopping. Practical value.
12. **"Why not just use a reasoning model?"** → QwQ-32B: C0<5%, SICA≡SC.
13. **"Random tiebreak baseline"** → exp-003: SICA tiebreak 80% vs random 50%.
14. **"Method improvement is incremental"** → Grounded in diagnosis (independence + taxonomy), not ad-hoc.
15. **"Weighted SC is simpler"** → exp-016 planned. Weighted SC doesn't address independence.
16. **"Within-model ICL transition contradicts regime theory"** → exp-050b (SC=57.79%, Δ=-3.52pp): ICL changes trace generation characteristics, not just SC level. Paper must distinguish "same model, different prompt" from "same model, same prompt, different accuracy."

## Working Title
**"Beyond Self-Consistency: How Trace Independence Limits Symbolic Consensus in LLM Reasoning"**
(Alternatives:
- "The Independence Bottleneck: Why Self-Extracted Symbolic Constraints Cannot Beat Majority Voting"
- "Symbolic Consensus Under the Condorcet Lens: Independence, Extraction, and the Limits of Self-Aggregation")

NOTE (Dream D037): Title MUST be scoped to "self-extracted constraints" / "SICA". Published methods (DyLoS, Aristotle, FoVer) use different approaches.

## Paper Structure (EMNLP 8pp + appendix)

### Main Tables
- T1: Main Results — models × domains, SC% / SICA% / Δpp / p-value, regime boundary
- T2: Oracle Control — Gold-FOL+MAX-SAT vs SC vs SICA-self, causal separation
- T3: Independence Quantification — Fleiss' κ / Eff-K / trace agreement per model
- T4: Extraction Error Taxonomy — trivially_satisfied / discriminative / both_wrong rates
- T5: Method Improvement — baseline SICA vs multi-temp vs filtered vs combined (⚠️ pending)

### Main Figures
- F1: Method Pipeline (SICA + multi-temp + filtering)
- F2: SC Accuracy vs SICA Δ scatter (hero figure, regime boundary)
- F3: K Sensitivity with diversity metrics (K vs Δ, K vs Eff-K)
- F4: Extraction error breakdown (stacked bar)

### Appendix
- K ablation details, temperature sensitivity, per-domain results, overhead analysis
- Entropy-conditioned analysis (continuous scatter + bin sensitivity)
- Six remediation strategy details
- Confirmation bias quantification
- Seed replication analysis
- QwQ-32B / DeepSeek-R1 negative control

## Claim Risk Notes (D059)
- **Seed replication unstable**: 2/3 positive but exp-053 null. Acknowledge, frame as motivation for method improvement.
- **Method claims PENDING**: exp-055/056 results determine Claims 5-6. If both fail → pure analysis paper.
- **Condorcet novelty**: Verify no prior work applies Condorcet independence to SC/SICA. WebSearch needed.
- **exp-050b complication**: ICL transition Δ=-3.52pp at SC=57.79% complicates simple "SC determines SICA." Explain via trace generation characteristic change.
- **Variable naming inconsistency**: 56.4% cross-trace pairs share zero Z3 variables. Key mechanism evidence.

## Required Citations (minimum 30 references)

- **SC & extensions**: Wang et al. 2023 (SC), Chen et al. 2023 (USC), Loo et al. 2025 (SC scaling plateaus), Taubenfeld et al. 2025 (weighted SC), DiVeRSe (Li et al. 2023)
- **Neuro-symbolic reasoning**: DyLoS (EACL 2026), Aristotle (ACL 2025), FoVer (TACL 2025), LogicAgent (2025), Logic-LM (Pan et al. 2023), LINC (Olausson et al. 2023)
- **Condorcet/voting theory**: Condorcet 1785, Austen-Smith & Banks 1996, relevant applications to ML ensembles
- **Test-time compute**: Snell et al. 2025, DeepSeek-R1, Diversity-Aware Training
- **Verification & reranking**: ORM (Cobbe et al. 2021), PRM (Lightman et al. 2023), Math-Shepherd
- **Constraint satisfaction**: SATBench (EMNLP 2025), LLM Meets Constraint Propagation (IJCAI 2025)
- **Debate & multi-agent**: Liang et al. 2023, Du et al. 2023

## Claim Scoping Rules
- n=60 conditions: "suggestive/consistent with" NOT "confirming"
- n≥200 conditions: can "confirm"
- Combined N>1,300: acceptable if breakdown clearly stated
- Method claims: must show statistically significant improvement OR clear directional improvement with analysis
- "Independence bottleneck" framing: systematic quantification + theoretical grounding

# Writing Plan — symb_invariant_consensus
# Generated: 2026-05-19T14:00:00Z
# Full Draft: D059 Independence Bottleneck + Method Improvement (dual contribution)
# Replaces: D057 Goldilocks Zone / old pure-negative framing
# Paper Agent Step 1 output

meta:
  venue: EMNLP 2026
  track: main
  template: templates/latex/acl/
  template_note: "ACL template shared by EMNLP; confirm 2026 style options when official EMNLP 2026 CFP releases"
  page_limit: 8
  deadline: 2026-05-25
  title: >
    Beyond Self-Consistency: How Trace Independence Limits
    Symbolic Consensus in LLM Reasoning
  core_claim: >
    Self-consistency's theoretical basis (Condorcet Jury Theorem) requires voter
    independence, but same-model sampling severely violates this assumption
    (Fleiss' κ>0.5, Effective-K only 1–2 for nominal K=12). Oracle control
    (+14.22pp) proves the aggregation mechanism works, but self-extracted
    constraints capture only 35% of this ceiling. Extraction error taxonomy
    reveals 43.1% trivially-satisfied constraints. Based on this diagnosis,
    we propose multi-temperature sampling (↑ trace diversity) and discriminative
    constraint filtering (↓ trivially-satisfied constraints).
  paper_type: "Analysis + Method Improvement (dual contribution)"
  framing: "Independence Bottleneck (Condorcet) + targeted interventions"
  created_at: 2026-05-19T14:00:00Z

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contributions (6, C5–C6 pending validation)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
contributions:
  - id: C1
    label: "Independence Bottleneck"
    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >
      Condorcet Jury Theorem requires voter independence; same-model traces
      violate this (Mistral κ=0.501 Eff-K=1.82, Qwen κ=0.739 Eff-K=1.31).
      Effective-K quantifies how many truly independent traces K samples provide.
    evidence: "§5.1, Table 3, Figure 3"

  - id: C2
    label: "Oracle Gap — Extraction Bottleneck"
    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >
      Gold FOL + MAX-SAT = +14.22pp (p=2.0e-7) FOLIO, +11.50pp PW. Self-extraction
      captures only 35% of oracle ceiling. Aggregation mechanism sound; extraction
      quality is the binding bottleneck.
    evidence: "§4.3, Table 1 (oracle rows)"
